title: Workspace Purpose
applicability: Introduces the purpose of the 2D state-event procedure design workspace in BestNameYet/Terminals.
purpose: Design and document an MCP-based interactive procedure with nonce-keyed persistent execution records, keyword-addressed projection definitions and accepted inputs, deterministic transitions through state.next, two interactive queue phases, and a complete persisted run record. The same nonce identifies the current saved state and projection until that procedure terminates.

title: Machine-Dialect Requirements for Workspace Agent Instructions
applicability: Every current and future entry, including nested instructional members and examples, in workspaces/2d-state-event-procedure-design/AGENTS.json.
required_behavior: Write and interpret every entry in this AGENTS.json according to both the explicit requirements and the spirit of machine dialect: preserve complete intended behavioral meaning, describe scope and required actions unambiguously, and provide enough operational context for an agent to interpret each instruction without guessing. Apply the complete authoritative definition reproduced verbatim below, including all of its writing requirements, contrastive examples, and validation criteria.

title: Nonce-Persisted Procedure States and Keyword-Bound Return Schemas
applicability: Governs the design, implementation, extension, validation, execution, queuing, resumption, and testing of every procedure-machine state, event, step file, instruction and schema pair, transition handler, and associated context exchange developed in this workspace.

architectural_definition.dimensions: The execution state is identified by a procedure nonce and a semantic state keyword; no persistent numeric step index or keyword-index map is required. A keyword addresses a projection definition and its process handler independently of position.
architectural_definition.state: A nonce retrieves the active execution record, including state.keyword, state.next, its already generated state.projection with final_schema, and accepted inputs by keyword. A state handler generates a projection from an addressable definition and previously accepted keyword values, or validates new input against the saved final_schema.
architectural_definition.event: E_RETURN(input) is a separate agent submission after the projection has been rendered. It contains an object under exactly the current state keyword; its presence does not itself signify acceptance.
architectural_definition.function_pointer: The controller dispatches input processing by record.state.keyword to the corresponding state-specific handler. The projection builder resolves the keyword-addressed definition, process handler, and optional schema-derivation function reference; no steps[i] lookup is used.
architectural_definition.context_object: The nonce-persisted record.inputs stores previously accepted values by independent semantic keyword. Projection generation resolves required earlier values there. Each agent call submits only the current keyword, and a rejection diagnostic is attached to the current stored projection without a pending separate control state.
architectural_definition.transition: Validate the submitted input against record.state.projection.final_schema and applicable semantic constraints. On rejection, keep the current state and its unchanged instruction and final_schema, add a diagnostic, persist, and render. On acceptance, store record.inputs[state.keyword], generate the successor named by state.next, save the same nonce record, and render its projection. A null successor marks completion.
architectural_definition.initialization: Starting with no procedure arguments generates a unique nonce and the initial verbatim_request projection, saves the record, then renders the projection. Invoking with only an existing nonce returns the saved projection unchanged; invoking with nonce and input processes that current input.
architectural_definition.persistence_and_handoff: Persist the nonce, current state keyword and successor, full generated projection and final_schema, all accepted keyword values, and continuity across queue handoff, suspension, and resumption. Keep each procedure independent by nonce; do not recalculate the schema on replay.

mandatory_behavior.non_deviation: Every procedure state, input, validation, retry, rendering action and queue continuation must use the nonce-persisted execution record and keyword-addressed state definitions. Do not reintroduce indexed iterator advancement, persistent keyword index maps, agent-selected destinations, or rendering coupled to receiving input.
mandatory_behavior.schema_contracts: Present the complete instruction and concrete JSON return schema for the current keyword. The agent supplies only that keyword. The generated final_schema is stored in the nonce record and used unchanged for input validation and nonce-only replay.
mandatory_behavior.handler_contracts: The state-specific handler validates submitted input against the saved final_schema and its semantic requirements, returning validity and any diagnostic. Projection generation, not rendering, resolves prior accepted input and the schema-derivation function. The controller persists and selects the successor by state.next.
mandatory_behavior.continuity: Accepted inputs must remain available as record.inputs[keyword] under independent stable addresses. Later procedure, simulation, execution and diagnostic representations preserve their original change-to-action associations and decorate them rather than creating disconnected lists.
mandatory_behavior.prohibited_substitution: Select the successor from the current saved state.next after acceptance, never by numeric index, input-supplied state name, or event column. A rejected input retains the same active state and final_schema.

dispatch_notation.table_cell: record.state.keyword is the current keyword and record.state.next is its successor keyword or null.
dispatch_notation.invocation: f(agentInput, nonce, {load,save,render}) loads the execution record; with no input it replays the saved projection, and with input it validates and saves either a diagnostic retry or the generated successor.
dispatch_notation.interpretation: Step order is expressed by keyword-addressed next references; a keyword permanently identifies the corresponding full instruction, return schema and applicable validator regardless of physical file placement.

examples.title: Initialization and accepted first return
sequence: A no-argument Procedure invocation creates a nonce and the initial verbatim_request state projection, persists it, then returns that projection.
The agent submits {verbatim_request: ...} with the same nonce in a later invocation.
The handler validates the saved final_schema, the controller records the accepted value and generates user_intent from state.next under the same nonce.

examples.title: Rejected input stays at the same index
sequence: With record.state.keyword equal to clarifying_questions, the agent submits an invalid clarifying_questions value.
The state-specific handler rejects the input and supplies a structured diagnostic.
The controller attaches the diagnostic to the same stored projection, preserves the unchanged instruction and final_schema, saves the record, and renders it again.

examples.title: Read accepted values by keyword
sequence: The nonce record stores accepted verbatim_request and user_intent values under their original keywords.
The clarifying_questions projection builder retrieves those values by keyword from record.inputs.
A validated reply adds only the clarifying_questions value to the same record.

examples.title: Simulation validation
sequence: The simulation_results projection is generated using execution_procedure and desired_state read by keyword.
Its final_schema, including derived constraints, is persisted before rendering.
A later nonce-plus-input invocation validates the stored schema and either persists a diagnostic retry or generates execution_results.

examples.title: Queue continuation
sequence: The application preserves the nonce-keyed record, previously accepted values, complete current projection, and history as required for queue handoff.
The resumed agent calls the procedure with its nonce and receives the identical current projection.
Its subsequent nonce-plus-input response is validated against the stored final_schema before advancing through state.next.

conformance_test: Conformance requires nonce-keyed persistence of the complete current projection and accepted inputs, full keyword-addressed instructions and schemas, state-specific validation against saved final_schema, deterministic state.next transitions, same-state diagnostic retry, and unchanged nonce-only replay.

title: State Tool-Response Input Instructions and JSON Return-Schema Alignment
applicability: Every state rendered to an agent through the MCP-based indexed procedure machine, including initial entry, re-entry after validation errors, queue-resumed interactions, and subsequent procedure phases.

model_definition.state_meaning: State_i(e) denotes a state object generated by an iterator-invoked state function. The state checks e.error before selecting normal or additive error mode, preserves pending diagnostics in the returned object, clears the error indicator, and references externally stored instructions and JSON return schema. The renderer resolves references without deciding mode or progression.
model_definition.expected_input: The agent returns one object containing the keyword requested by the active step. The run retains accepted values under their semantic keywords. A retry requests a corrected value under the same keyword.
model_definition.two_required_presentations: Every rendered state presents its expected input in two consistent forms: (1) a complete machine-dialect instruction in sentences and (2) a syntactically valid JSON return schema. Both presentations are authored in addressable external configuration files, selected by references contained in the state object, and assembled by the renderer. Neither is hardcoded as display text inside a script.
model_definition.input_contract_boundary: The iterator calls the active state function once per attempt. The state function prepares the state object and calls a separate renderer, which resolves and presents the instruction and its corresponding schema. The state function validates the subsequent E_RETURN(input) against that same schema before returning its validation result.

mandatory_behavior.machine_dialect_statement: For each state, generate a sentence-form instruction applying machine-dialect requirements to identify the input being requested, the values the agent must derive or preserve, their relationships to earlier accepted values referenced by keyword, and any relevant cardinality, identity, ordering, or allowed-value constraints. The statement must be sufficiently complete for an agent to construct the requested return without inferring undocumented meanings.
mandatory_behavior.valid_json_return_schema: In the same rendered tool response, display a real, syntactically valid JSON return schema as JSON, not pseudo-JSON, TypeScript notation, abbreviated field declarations, or an unexplained example payload. The schema must specify the expected object structure, data types, required properties, and applicable structural constraints so the submitted agent return can be validated.
mandatory_behavior.mandatory_sentence_for_every_nontrivial_: For every non-trivial key present anywhere in the JSON return schema, including nested object properties and array-item properties, the machine-dialect instruction statement must include at least one complete sentence explaining that key's intended value and expected input shape. The explanation must state what belongs in the field, not merely repeat the field name or JSON type. For worked examples illustrating complete sentence-form explanations of schema keys, including nested object properties and array-item properties, use the state instruction and return-schema pairs in the referenced workspace file: https://github.com/BestNameYet/Terminals/blob/main/workspaces/2d-state-event-procedure-design/state-instructions-and-return-schemas.json. The referenced examples illustrate this requirement and do not replace the instruction or schema for the current runtime state.
mandatory_behavior.cross_representation_alignment: The machine-dialect statement and the displayed JSON return schema must describe the same expected agent input. Every required field, nested relationship, array size limitation, enumeration, identifier reference, and other significant schema constraint must be represented consistently in the statement; no statement may request a structurally incompatible return and no schema may silently impose an unexplained non-trivial requirement.
mandatory_behavior.full_context_preservation: Require only the current keyword in the rendered return schema. Retrieve earlier accepted values with read(keyword) from the run's source. Retry the same keyword with the unchanged instruction and schema and an additive diagnostic.
mandatory_behavior.validation_responsibility: The active state function validates the currently requested value against the issued schema and applicable semantic constraints. A missing prerequisite from read(keyword) is an implementation error, distinct from a rejected agent reply.
mandatory_behavior.nonconformance: A rendered state is nonconforming when it omits either required input presentation, displays invalid JSON as the return schema, leaves a non-trivial schema key without a sentence-form explanation, or gives machine-dialect and schema definitions that disagree. Correct the rendered state contract before treating it as an acceptable procedure-machine state.
mandatory_behavior.instruction_schema_pair: Give each instruction and its expected return schema a shared semantic keyword within the procedure. When rendering the instruction, resolve its schema by that keyword and issue the two together. Validate the subsequent input against the same schema that was issued, including any constraints derived for that interaction. The pair is identified by its keyword regardless of where either definition is stored or where the step appears in the procedure.

examples.title: Clarifying questions use one keyword
examples.rendered_machine_dialect_instruction: Read `verbatim_request` and `user_intent`. Return `clarifying_questions` as an array of 7–11 questions necessary to fulfill the request. Each `id` is a unique stable question identifier such as Q1. Each `question` is a complete interrogative sentence.

displayed_json_return_schema.description: Response object containing the current state input under the semantic keyword clarifying_questions. Earlier accepted inputs remain in the iterator's separate indexed records.

clarifying_questions.description: The `clarifying_questions` property is an array containing between seven and eleven question objects needed to fulfill the user request.

items.description: Each object in `clarifying_questions` represents one question and contains its identifier and full question text.

id.description: The `clarifying_questions[].id` property is a string uniquely identifying the question, such as Q1.

question.description: The `clarifying_questions[].question` property is a string containing a complete interrogative sentence identifying information needed to fulfill the request.

examples.implementation_interpretation: The state retrieves verbatim_request and user_intent by keyword and gives those values to the separate renderer as needed. The reply contains only clarifying_questions. The same state function checks identifier uniqueness in addition to JSON Schema validation.

examples.title: Nonconforming unexplained nested key
examples.explanation: This example violates the rule because the sentence does not explain what execution_order means, how the integer relates to other steps, or what the identifiers in action_ids reference. These meanings must be explained in complete sentences alongside the schema.

title: Deterministic Event-Driven State Transitions and Context Argument Passing
applicability: Every transition, agent-submitted event, event/context property, selected function, and state invocation in the interactive indexed procedure machine, including validation retries and transitions between queue phases.

definitions.ordered_deterministic_route: The procedure follows zero-based indexed states. The current index i is advanced by exactly one when the current step's Function_i returns true and retained when it returns false. Both outcomes deterministically invoke next(e).
definitions.agent_event: E_RETURN(input) identifies the agent's reply to the active state. Its payload is the object containing the current keyword.
definitions.context_address: An accepted input is addressed by its semantic keyword in the run's source. For example, read('verbatim_request') retrieves the accepted original prompt.
definitions.selected_function: The iterator invokes the step file at index i. Its state function calls the renderer and validates the reply for the current keyword.
definitions.state_arguments: Give the state function access to read(keyword), the renderer, and any run-local control data required for a diagnostic. Do not require a complete context object.

mandatory_behavior.deterministic_transition_order: After the active state function returns a Boolean result, update i by Number(valid). Acceptance advances once and rejection retries the same index with the pending diagnostic.
mandatory_behavior.agent_input_drives_events: Treat the agent's response to a rendered state's instruction and JSON return schema as the event input. The agent supplies e; the event does not itself select a transition or encode validation success or failure.
mandatory_behavior.unique_specified_input_addresses: Assign each requested input a stable semantic keyword. Preserve earlier accepted values in the run's source under their existing keywords.
mandatory_behavior.function_event_argument: Deliver E_RETURN(input) to the active state function. It validates the current input and resolves any previously accepted values it needs by keyword.
mandatory_behavior.function_controls_next_state: Function_i controls the validation outcome but does not directly choose or invoke a destination state. Its true/false return is the sole input to the iterator's prescribed one-step advance or same-state retry; the iterator makes the index transition.
mandatory_behavior.state_receives_derived_arguments: Read only the prior accepted inputs required for the current step. Snapshot and clear any pending diagnostic and supply the separate renderer with the state object.
mandatory_behavior.initial_invocation_contract: On a new run the iterator starts at index zero. On resumption it starts at the saved index with access to earlier accepted values by keyword.

examples.title: Accepted input advances exactly once
sequence: The iterator selects the verbatim_request step.
The step calls the renderer and validates the reply under verbatim_request.
The iterator stores the accepted value and advances to user_intent.

examples.title: Validation retry does not change event type
sequence: The clarifying_questions step receives an invalid reply.
The state function returns false with a diagnostic.
The iterator invokes the same step again; the state function supplies the diagnostic to the renderer.

examples.title: Previous values remain available by keyword
sequence: The question_answers step reads clarifying_questions by keyword.
It derives the return schema from the accepted questions, then calls the separate renderer.
It validates only the question_answers reply against the issued schema and retains the original questions in the run's source.

conformance: Each selected state function calls a separate renderer and validates the current input. The iterator alone advances or retries. Earlier accepted input is recoverable by keyword.
implementation_choice_status: The selected implementation is zero-based indexed iterator advancement. Earlier direct state-invocation and deferred next-state-pointer examples are superseded; neither is an implementation alternative to this contract.

title: State-Event Transition Function Invocation and Explicit State Arguments
applicability: Every dispatch of an agent-return event to a transition function, its return-schema validation, and its invocation or return of a destination state in the interactive indexed function-pointer procedure machine.

architectural_contract.intersection_selection: The current step file at index i provides Function_i for the input requested by that step's instruction.
architectural_contract.event_consumption: The state function receives the current reply and accesses earlier accepted values by keyword when necessary.
architectural_contract.validation: Validate the reply against the exact issued schema and applicable semantics. Return true on acceptance or false with a diagnostic on rejection.
architectural_contract.invalid_response_route: On rejection, preserve the diagnostic for the next invocation and return false. The next attempt calls the renderer with that diagnostic and the same instruction and schema.
architectural_contract.valid_response_route: On acceptance, return true with the accepted input. The iterator advances exactly once and invokes the next step file.
architectural_contract.functional_argument_passing: Use a run-scoped keyword lookup for accepted values. Keep diagnostic control data separate from the agent payload.
architectural_contract.startup_defaults: Start at index zero on a new run or at the saved index on resumption with the same keyword source.
architectural_contract.deferred_or_immediate_invocation: The state function returns a validation result. The iterator alone selects and invokes the next step by index.

mandatory_behavior.deterministic_selection: Use the current step file's Function_i to determine the Boolean from the returned input and the schema issued with that step's instruction. The agent's return does not determine the Boolean or choose a destination.
mandatory_behavior.schema_validation_and_retry: The active state function validates the reply for its current keyword against the issued schema. Return a rejection diagnostic when validation fails.
mandatory_behavior.separate_context_and_state_argument: Provide read(keyword) for earlier accepted values and supply only the state-specific rendering data to the renderer.
mandatory_behavior.no_global_state_dependency: Scope keyword reads to the active run. Keep persisted position and validation diagnostics under run control.
mandatory_behavior.initial_state_defaults: The iterator starts with an empty accepted-value source for a new run unless the run has a saved position and source.

examples.title: One state callable uses a separate renderer
examples.explanation: The renderer resolves and presents the instruction and schema. The state function receives and validates the reply. In the procedure, the state also supplies any pending diagnostic and formats failures as structured diagnostic data.

examples.title: The iterator controls the next index
examples.javascript:
const result = await steps[i](e, i, read, exchange);
i += Number(result.valid);
examples.explanation: The active state function determines validity. The iterator advances for true or repeats for false.

conformance: Each step has one callable which invokes the separate renderer and validates the current keyword reply. The iterator uses the returned Boolean to advance or repeat.

title: Agent Return and Accepted Inputs by Keyword
applicability: Applies to agent replies and to the run-scoped source of previously accepted inputs.

requirements.title: Event representation
requirements.required_behavior: Represent an agent submission as E_RETURN(input), where input contains only the value under the keyword requested by the current step.

requirements.title: Unique input addresses
requirements.required_behavior: Assign each independently recallable input its own semantic keyword. Resolve earlier accepted values through read(keyword).

requirements.title: Context accumulation
requirements.required_behavior: After acceptance, record the new value by keyword in the active run. Keep earlier accepted values intact. Keep retry diagnostics separate from accepted inputs.

requirements.title: Property ownership
requirements.required_behavior: For each step document the one keyword the agent supplies. The state function invokes the renderer and then validates the reply against the schema issued for that keyword.

example.title: Keyword-addressed agent replies
sequence: The agent returns {verbatim_request: ...} and the run records it by keyword.
The user_intent step reads verbatim_request and calls the renderer.
The agent returns {user_intent: ...}.
The same step validates the reply and the iterator records user_intent separately.

title: File-Level Change Mapping as the Procedure's Structural Foundation
applicability: The procedure-design phase that compares the current system state with the user-requested desired final system state, identifies filesystem changes, identifies agent actions, maps the actions to those changes, and subsequently expands the mappings into a procedure.
purpose: Ensure that the procedure specifies concrete, individually identifiable file changes and the agent actions that produce each change, rather than producing an abstract action list disconnected from the desired final state.

required_behavior.file_level_granularity: For each filesystem transformation required by the desired final system state, describe the change at the level of the specific file affected. Give each separately identifiable file change its own change identifier, specify the affected file path, and classify its operation as create, modify, or delete. Do not substitute a broad directory-level or project-level description when a specific file change can be identified.
required_behavior.desired_state_traceability: Identify which required condition or conditions of the desired final system state each file-level change is intended to satisfy. Preserve these relationships using the existing identifiers assigned to the final-state requirements and changes.
required_behavior.actions_per_change: For each defined file change, identify the exact agent action or actions needed to produce that change. Map the action identifiers to the corresponding file-change identifier so the procedure can independently recover which actions effect which file changes. An action may be referenced by multiple change mappings where it produces multiple independently identified file changes.
required_behavior.mapping_as_skeleton: Treat the existing change-to-action mappings as the canonical skeleton of the procedure. When generating ordered steps, command examples, code examples, simulation outputs, execution observations, or diagnostics, extend or decorate those mappings without replacing them with an unrelated action list, dropping original identifiers, or losing the link to the desired final state.
required_behavior.completion_coverage: Represent every required file-level change in the mapping and associate it with its necessary actions. Where a required file change or action remains unmapped, identify the gap rather than silently omitting the requirement.

example.scenario: The user's desired final state requires adding a new JSON configuration file and modifying an existing JavaScript program to read it.

actions.description: Write the required configuration data to config/settings.json.
Modify src/app.js so it reads config/settings.json and uses the configured values.

example.interpretation: The two file changes remain separately addressable and traceable to the desired final-state conditions. Subsequent procedure and simulation stages add execution details to these same mappings rather than replacing them.

title: Two-Phase Interactive MCP Procedure Queue and Agent Handoff
applicability: The application workflow that uses the indexed machine to develop a procedure with an initial agent, place the resulting procedure into a queue, and continue interactively with a second agent for review, execution, and post-execution diagnostics.
purpose: Establish that both sides of the queued handoff are interactive procedures, not an issue-comment job processor or an offline batch execution, so future queue design and implementation preserve the intended agent-facing MCP interaction.

required_behavior.first_phase_interactive_procedure: The first agent responds to successive states from index zero with the current requested keyword. Each active state function calls the separate renderer and validates the reply. The iterator advances on acceptance or retries on rejection. The agent identifies required changes, maps them to actions, builds a procedure and simulates its commands, code and predicted effects.
required_behavior.queue_handoff: After procedure preparation, queue the prepared procedure and continuation information with access to the same run's accepted values by keyword. Preserve file-change identifiers, action identifiers, mappings and accepted data for the second agent.
required_behavior.second_phase_interactive_procedure: The second agent receives the queued procedure and continues through its own interactive procedure exchanges. That phase comprises reviewing the prepared procedure, executing the associated actions, and completing the post-execution diagnostic against the existing desired-state requirements and checklist. The second agent's interactive responses remain subject to state-specific machine-dialect instructions, JSON return schemas, and function-selected transitions.
required_behavior.mcp_based_queue: Expose the queue and both interactive procedure phases through the application's MCP-based interface. Treat IssueStack's issue-backed queue only as historical design context, not as a required implementation or an execution dependency; an Issue-comment-triggered workflow is not a substitute for the intended interactive MCP queue.
required_behavior.preserve_machine_architecture: Preserve the ordered files, keyword-bound instruction and schema pairs, zero-based index, access to the run's accepted inputs, and Boolean-controlled advancement across queue transport, assignment, suspension, resumption and phase transfer.
required_behavior.retain_full_run: Ensure the application's complete run record encompasses both interactive phases, the queue handoff, actual execution results, and post-execution diagnostics. The queue must preserve continuity of the same procedure rather than treating the second phase as a new unrelated request.

example.title: Interactive procedure authoring followed by interactive review and execution
sequence: Agent 1 responds to each MCP-rendered step with that step's requested keyword. The active state function validates the reply.
Agent 1 produces a file-level change-to-action mapping and decorates that mapping with the stepwise procedure and a proposed simulation containing commands, code and predicted effects.
The application queues the prepared procedure, saved index and reference to the run's accepted inputs.
Agent 2 resumes at the saved index, retrieves earlier inputs by keyword, and continues the same run.
Agent 2 executes the reviewed procedure and interactively supplies actual execution observations and the decorated post-execution diagnostic checklist.
The application retains the complete record spanning both agents and the handoff.

implementation_boundary: This instruction specifies required queue behavior and relationships, not a queue storage format, claim protocol, scheduling policy, MCP tool naming convention, or specific implementation strategy. Those decisions must be made separately without changing the stated interactive two-phase behavior.

title: Runner, Step Selection, State-Object Renderer, and Two Interactive Applications
applicability: Architecture of the MCP-based procedure system, including starting a procedure, resolving step transitions, presenting state instructions, creating queued procedures, reviewing and executing queued jobs, post-execution review, and access to completed jobs.

runner.purpose: Coordinate the program lifecycle and the indexed iterator. The iterator, not a transition handler or renderer, is the sole controller of progression and retry, while the current step handles validation.
runner.required_behavior: Initialize or restore the zero-based index and access to the run's accepted-value source. Call the step at the current index once per attempt. Store accepted output by keyword and use the step's Boolean result to advance or retry.
runner.expected_interface: Supply the active step with read(keyword), the interaction service and run-local diagnostic access. Pass the agent's current reply to the running step through the interaction.

state_event_dispatcher.purpose: Select the step file using only the iterator index.
state_event_dispatcher.required_behavior: Invoke the selected state function once per attempt. Step selection does not change the index, render a state object, or validate a reply.
state_event_dispatcher.expected_interface: Use the current index to invoke the selected step and obtain its validation result for the iterator.

state_object_construction.purpose: Keep state-specific instruction and schema references separate from presentation.
state_object_construction.required_behavior: The state function reads required earlier values by keyword, snapshots and clears any pending diagnostic, constructs the state object, and calls the separate renderer with it. The same state function validates the subsequent reply using the schema issued by that interaction.
state_object_construction.expected_interface: Pass the renderer the state keyword, external content references or derived schema, and only the runtime data needed for this presentation.

renderer.purpose: Use a separate rendering function or script to transform a state object into the agent-facing tool response.
renderer.required_behavior: Resolve all external content references from the state object. In error mode, conspicuously display the diagnostic before the full unchanged normal state instruction and JSON schema. In normal mode, display the instruction and schema. Never decide validation or transitions or hardcode system-authored text.
renderer.expected_interface: Accept a state object containing content references and runtime values; load the referenced configuration values from files external to executable scripts and return or emit the rendered tool response. The exact configuration format, file paths, rendering format, and implementation language are undecided.

applications.minimum_separation: Implement at least two distinct applications using the shared procedure architecture. They must not be collapsed into a single indistinguishable workflow that obscures the two interactive queue phases.

procedure_creation_application.purpose: Provide the interactive application through which an agent creates a procedure to satisfy a user request.
procedure_creation_application.required_behavior: Present successive state instructions through the runner and renderer, collect agent return-schema responses, derive file-level changes and mapped agent actions, and develop and simulate the procedure. At the defined handoff it must make the prepared procedure available as a queued job, preserving its context and mappings.

job_review_execution_application.purpose: Provide the interactive application through which an agent accesses queued jobs, inspects their prepared procedures, carries out their actions, performs post-execution review, and accesses completed jobs.
job_review_execution_application.required_behavior: Display available queued jobs and permit selecting a job for interactive review and execution through state responses. Present the prepared procedure and retained context, run its execution phase, and conduct the post-procedure diagnostic. Mark the job complete according to the defined completion condition after post-execution review, and support listing and displaying completed jobs and their recorded results.

responsibility_boundaries.responsibility: Coordinate procedure startup, agent return handling, iterator and step calls, persistence and interactive application lifecycle.
Maintain the zero-based index, invoke one state function per attempt, record accepted input and apply the Boolean result.
Select the step file by the iterator index.
The active state function validates the current keyword reply against its issued schema and returns its Boolean result and any diagnostic.
Read required inputs by keyword, prepare the state object, and call the renderer before validating the reply.
Resolve referenced templates and schema; display error diagnostic before unchanged normal instruction when error mode is selected.
Display queued and completed jobs and interactively review, execute, diagnose and complete jobs.

illustrative_flow: The application initializes or restores the iterator index and the run's accepted-value source.
The active state function reads required earlier values, captures and clears any pending diagnostic, and passes the state object to the renderer.
The renderer resolves the state object's references and displays either the normal instruction and schema or a conspicuous diagnostic followed by that same complete normal instruction and schema.
The agent later returns the current keyword as E_RETURN(input). The same state function validates the reply against the schema issued with the instruction and returns its result to the iterator.
The iterator applies i += Number(valid), then invokes the step at the resulting index.
The creation application queues the prepared procedure with a reference to the run, preserving the accepted values, index, history and mappings.

The review/execution application uses the same iterator and step-selection behavior, records execution and post-execution diagnostics, and makes completed jobs available after defined completion conditions are satisfied.
unresolved_implementation_decisions: Do not infer a concrete programming language, module and script names, process topology, job-list presentation format, queue storage structure, job ownership policy, persistence serialization, or job-completion status protocol from this architectural entry. These details remain to be specified. This entry fixes component responsibilities and the minimum application separation without selecting those implementation details.

title: External Addressable Content and Reference-Only Rendering
applicability: Every script, module, state function, transition function, runner, dispatcher, renderer, and interactive application that creates or displays agent-facing tool responses or other system-generated interface text in this workspace.
purpose: Separate all rendered wording and configurable display content from executable scripts. Every displayed instruction, prompt, label, diagnostic, explanatory sentence, or other system-authored text must be stored in independently addressable configuration resources rather than hardcoded in program source.

definitions.rendered_text: Any system-authored text that a program causes the agent or job viewer to see, including state instructions, return-schema explanations, validation errors, display headings, labels, queue/job prompts and completion diagnostics. Dynamically echoed agent inputs or observed command output are runtime data, not hardcoded display templates.
definitions.external_content_resource: A configuration file outside the executable script that stores content entries under stable addresses or keys. The exact file paths, format, and organization are not specified by this requirement.
definitions.content_reference: A stable, resolvable identifier recorded in a state object or other rendering input that selects a content entry from an external resource. A content reference is an address, not embedded display text.
definitions.rendering_resolution: The renderer loads the externally configured content selected by the references, incorporates explicitly supplied runtime values where needed, and produces the displayed response without composing system-authored wording in code.

mandatory_behavior.absolute_prohibition_on_embedded_render_: Do not hardcode, declare, concatenate, interpolate, or store any system-authored rendered text directly inside an executable script. A script may contain identifiers, references, control flow, field names, and runtime data operations; it must not carry the user-facing wording that those identifiers select.
mandatory_behavior.external_configurable_storage: Store every system-authored rendered text value in an addressable, configurable file located outside the executable script. Each value must have a uniquely specified reference that the application can resolve when needed. Updating display wording must be possible through the configuration resource without editing executable script source.
mandatory_behavior.reference_only_state_objects: State_i(e) returns references to externally stored normal instruction and JSON schema, and when e.error indicates a pending failure, also supplies a reference to diagnostic presentation plus a copied diagnostic payload. It must capture the error before clearing it and never embed actual rendered wording in executable code.
mandatory_behavior.reference_only_diagnostics: On failed validation Function_i records e.error with error=true, an errortype that identifies externally addressable diagnostic content, and any structured data needed for substitution. State_i snapshots the error into its state object and clears the indicator. The renderer resolves the diagnostic reference; no rendered error sentence may be hardcoded in a script.
mandatory_behavior.renderer_resolves_references: The separate renderer resolves the normal instruction and schema in every mode. In additive error mode it additionally resolves the diagnostic reference and displays it conspicuously before the unchanged normal content. Missing content references are program errors; the renderer must not invent fallback sentences.
mandatory_behavior.all_applications_in_scope: Apply the same reference-only rendering rule to both the interactive procedure-creation application and the queued-job review/execution/completion application. This includes job lists, job selection, completed-job displays and post-execution review wording.
mandatory_behavior.external_schema_content: Where JSON return schemas or their explanatory text are displayed, store the displayed schema definitions and any explanatory copy in externally addressable configuration resources. State scripts identify the applicable schema by reference rather than embedding complete schema definitions in source.
mandatory_behavior.preserve_machine_dialect: Externally stored state instructions must still satisfy the machine-dialect writing rules, describe every non-trivial schema key in sentence form, and align with the referenced valid JSON return schema. Moving content into configuration does not relax the state-input contract.

example.title: State snapshots pending diagnostic and renderer resolves external content
example.interpretation: Only identifiers and control logic are in script. In error mode the externally supplied formatResponse configuration shows the resolved diagnostic before the full unchanged normal instruction and schema. The diagnostic remains available after e.error is cleared because the state captured it in the state object supplied to the separate renderer.

implementation_boundary: This entry requires reference-only configuration-driven rendering but does not decide which configuration file format, directory, resource loader, caching method, template engine or renderer implementation to use. Those decisions are separate from the non-negotiable prohibition on hardcoded rendered text.

title: Step Validation Functions and Iterator-Controlled State Invocation
applicability: Each step file, its Function_i, validation outcomes, error production and iterator-controlled State_i invocation in the two interactive procedure applications.
architecture_decision: Each step file provides one state callable. It calls a separate renderer and validates the current keyword reply against the exact schema issued with its instruction. The iterator advances or retries using the callable's Boolean result.

mandatory_behavior.dedicated_handler_per_cell: Every step supplies the returned input and the specific schema issued with its instruction to validation. A shared validation routine may check that pair without receiving or inferring the position of the step.
mandatory_behavior.invalid_input: On schema or applicable semantic validation failure, the state function returns false and a pending diagnostic with an externally configured type and structured details. The iterator retains the index.
mandatory_behavior.accepted_input: On successful validation, the state function returns true and the new accepted input. The iterator records that value and advances one index.
mandatory_behavior.state_builds_not_renders: The state function captures and clears a pending diagnostic, builds its state object with references and runtime data, and calls the separate renderer. Rendering the state object is the renderer's responsibility. The state function validates the resulting reply.
mandatory_behavior.renderer_outputs_state_object: The renderer displays resolved error material conspicuously before the full unchanged normal instruction and JSON schema when mode is error. It does not validate, change i, or choose a function pointer.
mandatory_behavior.preserve_reference_only_text: All displayed state instructions, error messages, schema content, labels and formatting are externally configured and addressed by reference. Function and state identifiers used for program control are not rendered instruction strings.
mandatory_behavior.procedure_specific_behavior: Validation functions contain only the validation and diagnostic logic applicable to their instruction and return-schema pairs. Their Boolean drives the iterator's only index branch, and no additional transition mechanisms are introduced without separate procedural specification.

illustrative_example.purpose: A single clarifying_questions invocation calls the renderer, validates the reply, and returns a result. The iterator controls the next invocation.
illustrative_example.interpretation: The example shows structural validation and the result shape. The state function also applies any applicable state-specific checks and supplies pending retry diagnostics to the renderer.

implementation_selection: The zero-based indexed iterator with Boolean-controlled state advancement replaces the former direct preceding/following state invocation design. Historical direct-call examples elsewhere are superseded and must be reconciled rather than treated as active alternatives.

title: Indexed Procedure Iterator, Boolean Validation Branching, and Additive Error-Mode Rendering
applicability: Every initialization, state invocation, agent-return event, validation operation, index transition, retry, state rendering, and procedure continuation governed by the indexed procedure in this workspace.
purpose: Define deterministic indexed step invocation and retry, with keyword access to accepted inputs and a single-use diagnostic on rejection.

definitions.iterator_index: The nonnegative integer i identifies the current procedure position. The initial index is zero. State_i and Function_i correspond to the same index i.
definitions.context_object: Accepted inputs are held in a run-scoped source and retrieved through read(keyword). Local control state may carry a pending diagnostic.
definitions.state_function: One callable at step index i prepares the state object, calls the renderer and validates the current reply.
definitions.validation_function: Validation occurs inside the active state function after rendering. The state function uses the issued schema and applicable semantic constraints and returns a Boolean result.
definitions.validation_boolean: The Boolean returned by Function_i is true when the requested input is accepted and false when rejected. This Boolean is determined by application validation rather than by the agent.
definitions.error_property: The property e.error is reserved for validation diagnostics. A populated error object identifies a failed validation and supplies error type and diagnostic information required for rendering.
definitions.normal_mode: The rendering mode that displays the complete ordinary instruction and JSON return schema associated with the current state.
definitions.error_mode: The rendering mode that conspicuously displays the pending validation diagnostic before the complete, unchanged normal instruction and JSON return schema for the same state.

mandatory_behavior.initialization: Initialize i at zero for a new run or restore the saved index and access to the run's accepted-value source.
mandatory_behavior.state_invocation: Invoke the state function at the current index once per attempt. The function reads prerequisites by keyword and calls the separate renderer with its state object.
mandatory_behavior.error_detection: At the beginning of State_i(e), inspect e.error. A populated validation error object with error=true selects error mode; an absent, null or cleared marker selects normal mode.
mandatory_behavior.error_snapshot_and_reset: Preserve a pending diagnostic in the state object before clearing its run-local value. Clearing it does not change the index or earlier accepted inputs.
mandatory_behavior.normal_rendering: In normal mode, construct a state object referencing the complete machine-dialect instruction and JSON return schema for State_i. The renderer resolves these from externally configured resources.
mandatory_behavior.error_rendering: In error mode, construct a state object referencing the same unchanged normal instruction and JSON return schema plus an additional conspicuous error presentation before them. Do not replace, abbreviate or modify the normal instruction or schema.
mandatory_behavior.agent_response: The reply arrives as E_RETURN(input) for the running state function. Its payload contains the current requested keyword and value. Validity is determined by the state function.
mandatory_behavior.function_selection: Select the step file at index i. The step provides Function_i and the return schema associated with its rendered instruction. Use only i_next to select the next step file after validation.
mandatory_behavior.input_validation: The active state function validates the current keyword against the issued schema and applicable semantic constraints.
mandatory_behavior.validation_success: Return true and the accepted input. The iterator records that input by keyword and advances exactly one index.
mandatory_behavior.validation_failure: Return false with a diagnostic including error=true, errortype and structured details as applicable. Keep it available for the next attempt.
mandatory_behavior.index_retention: On false, retain i and invoke the same step. It captures and clears the pending diagnostic and calls the renderer for the retry.
mandatory_behavior.boolean_transition: Compute i_next=i+Number(valid), with true contributing 1 and false contributing 0. Neither agent input nor renderer may independently advance the index.
mandatory_behavior.recursive_continuation: After validation, choose the next step file by the resulting index. Each attempt requests the input for one semantic keyword.
mandatory_behavior.interaction_boundary: The state function calls the separate renderer to present its state object and awaits the subsequent agent reply. It then validates the reply within the same invocation. Rendering and receiving the reply are distinct interaction phases.
mandatory_behavior.context_preservation: Keep earlier accepted values in the run's keyword source. Rejections do not replace accepted values.
mandatory_behavior.function_responsibility_boundary: The state function calls the separate renderer, validates the reply and returns the result. It does not present the response itself, invoke a destination state, or modify the index.
mandatory_behavior.renderer_responsibility_boundary: The renderer resolves externally configured templates and schemas and produces output. It does not validate returns, select transition functions, change i, or independently determine error state.
mandatory_behavior.persistence_and_handoff: Preserve the run identity, iterator index, accepted-value source and pending diagnostic across suspension, queue handoff and resumption.
mandatory_behavior.non_deviation: Do not substitute direct destination-state calls, agent-chosen routing, validity-coded event types or monolithic conditional dispatch for Boolean-controlled index advancement. Use the step file's own instruction and return-schema pair.

interface_contracts.iterator_entry: The iterator selects steps[i] and calls it once per attempt.
interface_contracts.dispatch_entry: steps[i] identifies the step file. Its semantic keyword identifies the instruction and return-schema pair.
interface_contracts.validation_return: The state function returns { valid, input, error }. valid is a Boolean. input contains the accepted reply on success and is null on rejection. error contains the diagnostic on rejection and is null on success.

failure_error_shape.errortype: An identifier for an applicable externally configured validation diagnostic, with structured data as needed.

interface_contracts.continuation: After applying the Boolean result, invoke the step at the resulting index.

execution_examples.title: Initial successful validation
sequence: Start at index zero with no accepted values.
The verbatim_request step calls the renderer and receives the reply under its keyword.
The state function validates the reply and returns true with the input.
The iterator records the accepted value and advances to index one.

execution_examples.title: Failed validation and same-state retry
sequence: The clarifying_questions state receives an invalid reply.
The state function returns false with a diagnostic.
The iterator retries the same step.
The step captures and clears the diagnostic before calling the renderer.
The renderer presents it before the unchanged instruction and schema.

execution_examples.title: Successful correction after retry
sequence: The step receives a corrected reply containing clarifying_questions.
The state function validates the reply and returns true.
The iterator records the value and advances. The next step reads it by keyword.

relationship_to_existing_workspace_instr.preserved_requirements: Preserve indexed step selection, external rendering resources, keyword-addressed accepted values, aligned return schemas, Boolean-controlled transitions, persisted run records and the interactive two-phase queue.
relationship_to_existing_workspace_instr.superseded_transition_behavior: The active state function calls the separate renderer and validates its reply. The iterator alone invokes the following or repeated step.
relationship_to_existing_workspace_instr.superseded_index_convention: Use a zero-based index for step selection and semantic keywords for accepted values and schema lookup.
relationship_to_existing_workspace_instr.reconciliation_requirement: Maintain one authoritative iterator and transition mechanism across all current instruction objects and implementation examples; do not leave competing active direct-invocation contracts.

title: State Object Composition and Context-Derived Return Schemas
applicability: Every state function preparing a state object for the separate renderer, including validation-error retries.
purpose: Specify state-object components and allow derivation of a return schema from earlier accepted values read by keyword.

definitions.state_object: The JSON object constructed and returned by State_i(e) for the current state. It contains two mandatory content members, instruction and return_schema, and may contain one additional content member, error_message, when a validation diagnostic is pending.
definitions.instruction: The mandatory content member describing the current state's agent-facing instruction. Its system-authored wording is obtained through the externally configured content mechanism; it must not be hardcoded into the state function.
definitions.return_schema: The mandatory content member specifying the syntactically valid JSON return schema governing the input requested from the agent by the current state. The schema can be obtained from an external configured resource or derived at runtime by the state's schema helper using declared inputs from e.
definitions.error_message: The conditional content member containing or referencing the diagnostic for a pending validation failure. It accompanies, rather than replaces, the mandatory instruction and return_schema members.
definitions.state_local_schema_helper: An optional function defined within State_i that receives one or more specified properties of e and computes the current state's return schema from their accepted values. Its output is used as the return_schema component of the constructed state object.

mandatory_behavior.mandatory_components: State_i(e) must construct a JSON state object containing both instruction and return_schema on every invocation, whether or not a validation error exists. Neither component may be omitted, substituted by error_message, or replaced with a mere statement that the component will be produced later.
mandatory_behavior.conditional_error_component: Include error_message when e.error indicates a pending validation error. Capture the diagnostic needed for error presentation before clearing e.error according to the existing iterator rule. When no validation error exists, omit the error_message content member.
mandatory_behavior.normal_and_error_composition: A normal response includes instruction and return_schema. An error response includes error_message in addition to the same complete normal instruction and return_schema; the error message is displayed conspicuously before the normal instruction by the existing rendering mechanism.
mandatory_behavior.instruction_content_source: The instruction member must identify or carry the state-specific instruction obtained from externally addressable configuration content. Constructing the JSON state object does not authorize hardcoding any system-authored instruction wording in executable source.
mandatory_behavior.schema_source_selection: For each state invocation, supply a return_schema from either an externally configured schema definition or a dynamically constructed schema. Dynamic construction must produce a concrete, syntactically valid JSON Schema for the input requested at the current State_i, not an unexplained placeholder or abbreviated pseudo-schema.
mandatory_behavior.optional_state_local_helper: A State_i function may define a dedicated schema-construction helper inside its own function body. When used, the helper must receive one or more explicitly identified properties of e as inputs and derive the return_schema from their values. The helper is optional; the requirement does not force dynamic construction where an externally configured schema suffices.
mandatory_behavior.context_derivation: Use declared inputs retrieved by keyword to derive the applicable fields, types and constraints. Preserve earlier accepted values.
mandatory_behavior.schema_instruction_alignment: The instruction and schema describe the same one-keyword response. Any derived constraints come from the accepted values retrieved by keyword. The state function validates the reply against the schema issued with that instruction.
mandatory_behavior.separate_rendering_responsibility: The state function constructs the state object, supplies it to the separate renderer, and validates the later reply. The renderer resolves and presents the content.
mandatory_behavior.preserve_existing_architecture: The indexed iterator governs step order, and the semantic keyword identifies the instruction and return-schema pair. State-object composition and schema derivation follow the existing Boolean validation, single-use diagnostic and external-content contracts.

composition_examples.title: Normal state object

content_members.instruction: Reference or resolved value of the externally configured state instruction

composition_examples.interpretation: The instruction and JSON return schema are present; error_message is omitted because no validation error is pending. The schema is illustrative content, not an instruction to hardcode it into executable source.

composition_examples.title: Error-mode state object

content_members.instruction: Reference or resolved value of the same externally configured state instruction
content_members.error_message: Reference or resolved diagnostic captured from e.error

composition_examples.interpretation: The pending diagnostic is additional to the two mandatory components. The renderer places the diagnostic conspicuously before the unchanged normal instruction and schema.

composition_examples.title: State-local helper deriving a schema from context
composition_examples.interpretation: The state reads accepted clarifying_questions by keyword, derives the question_answers schema, and calls the separate renderer. The reply contains question_answers and is checked against the issued schema.

conformance: A state object conforms when it always contains instruction and a valid return_schema; includes error_message only when a pending diagnostic exists; preserves the full normal instruction and schema in error mode; and uses external content references or runtime derivation rather than hardcoding rendered instruction, diagnostic, or fixed schema content in executable code.
